$comment: THE declarative source for both the layer contract and its test matrix. scripts/validate-rules.mjs generates a source x target cross-product from `layers`: every pair listed in `mayImport` must lint clean, every pair NOT listed must error. Hand-picked fixture samples let real gaps through — that is why this is a table, not a list of examples. Keep it in step with references/placement/layers-and-imports.md.
$note_roots: `root` is the layer ROOT (what lint scopes to); `dir` is a representative slice inside it (what the matrix writes fixtures into). They differ because a permission is granted to a layer but exercised through a slice. `read` nests inside `inbound`, so the resolved-path config must exclude it from the parent zone target — nesting is derived from these paths, never hand-listed.
$note_ports: `ports` is its own top-level layer, `src/ports/**`. A use-case owns the contract and an outbound adapter implements it, so both must reach it while neither may reach the other's implementation — which is only expressible in lint if the contract is not nested inside either.

$note_tiers: `mayImportAt` grants an edge at named modules only — `app` may reach `client-cache` at its `prefetch` entry and nowhere else. `resolvedOnly: true` marks a case the string tier provably cannot see (a subpath carve-out, or a specifier assembled at runtime): it must lint CLEAN under `eslint-boundaries.mjs` alone and ERROR once `eslint-boundaries-resolved.mjs` is present. That keeps the two tiers in a subset relation instead of letting them contradict each other.
$note_specimens: Specimens are subpath-precise on purpose. Certifying `use-cases -> infrastructure` with a generic module would grant the whole layer, while the contract permits only the boundary wrapper; `app -> client-cache` likewise means the prefetch entry, not browser queries.
$note_surfaces: A use-case slice has two surfaces and they are separate layers, not a naming convention. `operations/**` reaches domain, ports and data, throws typed failures and reports nothing — it may NOT reach `boundary/**`, which is what stops an operation from quietly becoming a second declaration. `entries/**` reaches the combinator and operations, and may NOT reach data or ports directly, which is what stops a declaration from skipping the operation it wraps. Inbound adapters reach entries only. NOT enforced here: that an entry calls its OWN slice's operation. Relating a source slice to a target slice needs slice identity, which a portable table does not have — same limit as slice isolation, and recorded the same way in rules/README.md.

selfRules.message: A declaration never calls another declaration — compose the operation it wraps, so the failure is reported once at the outermost boundary.
